title: Measures to Deter Bullying in Schools
what_it_is: Measures to Deter Bullying in Schools

sections.label: Physical bullying and school response
sections.summary: Physical bullying was less prevalent at about 5%, and MOE does not tolerate bullying, with staff counselling students involved and affected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Physical bullying was less prevalent at about 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE does not tolerate bullying in any form and every child has a right to feel safe and secure in our schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: School staff will also counsel students who are involved in bullying as well as those affected by it.

sections.label: Cyberbullying definition and school support
sections.summary: Cyberbullying is defined as hostile or aggressive messages sent through electronic or digital media, and schools have prevention and intervention measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Cyberbullying is defined as any behaviour performed through electronic or digital media by individuals or groups that communicate hostile or aggressive messages intended to inflict harm or discomfort over time against a victim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In terms of support, the schools have put in place bullying prevention and intervention measures, such as providing accessible channels for safe reporting of bullying cases, investigating and following up promptly on reported cases, and, as I was saying in reply to Assoc Prof Daniel Goh earlier, adopting an educational approach to help all students, including bystanders, to learn from the incidents and prevent further bullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In severe cases, parents and child will be with the school to look at how the incident can be dealt with and how follow-up actions can be taken together − by the school, the student and the parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Organisations, like the Children's Society, are also in touch with our schools to extend further help and general education to students and parents.

sections.label: Hotline reporting data and bullying stability
sections.summary: The Minister does not have data on hotline reporting patterns and says bullying has been stable and managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: At the moment, I do not have the data on the patterns of the hotline reporting, and if the Member would like to file a Parliamentary Question (PQ) on that, then we can give the Member more details on the patterns, if there are any.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But on the whole, bullying, as I have mentioned in the PQ reply, has been stable and managed.
